'''Martin Allen Brumbaugh''' was an American statistician, economist and educator. He was a professor at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] and the [[University of Buffalo]]. He was a pioneer of [[statistical process control]] and a founding member of the [[American Society for Quality Control]].

==Early life==
Martin Allen Brumbaugh was born to Mary (née Haffley) and Irvin G. Brumbaugh. His father was a merchant in Pennsylvania and his uncle [[Martin G. Brumbaugh]] was Pennsylvania governor.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/altoona-tribune-irvin-g-brumbaugh-1-se/175057358/ |title=Irvin G. Brumbaugh |date=1943-09-01 |newspaper=Altoona Tribune |page=10 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref><ref name="alumni">{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-buffalo-news-buffalo-doctor-elected/175035065/ |title=Buffalo Doctor Elected |date=1943-06-01 |newspaper=Buffalo Evening News |page=19 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref> He graduated from [[Juniata College]] in 1918.<ref name="alumni"/> He attended post graduate courses at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] and [[Northwestern University]].<ref name="buffalo">{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-buffalo-news-dr-m-a-brumbaugh-joi/175021240/ |title=Dr. M. A. Brumbaugh Joins U. of B. Staff |date=1929-09-09 |newspaper=Buffalo Evening News |page=9 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref> His 1926 dissertation at the University of Pennsylvania was entitled "Direct Method of Determining Cyclical Fluctuations of Economic Data".<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.nber.org/system/files/chapters/c0685/c0685.pdf |title=Business Cycles: The Problem and Its Setting |last=Mitchell |first=Wesley Clair |year=1927 |pages=477–478 |via=nber.org |access-date=2025-06-22}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1922, Brumbaugh became an assistant professor of economics and statistics at the [[Wharton School]] of the University of Pennsylvania. From 1926 to 1927, he was chief statistician of a study of conditions in Pennsylvania state and county institutions. In September 1929, he became a professor of statistics and economics at the School of Business Administration at the [[University of Buffalo]].<ref name="buffalo"/> From 1928 to 1929, he was involved in surveying the [[worsted]] yarn industry for the spinners' division of the [[Wool Institute]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-buffalo-news-professor-at-u-of-b-t/175021672/ |title=Professor at U. of B. to Report Yarn Data |date=1929-10-07 |newspaper=Buffalo Evening News |page=21 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref>

In 1929, Brumbaugh described the U.S. tax system as a "socialistic force" and was surging the inequality of incomes.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-buffalo-news-present-tax-system-in-u/175033100/ |title=Present Tax System in U.S. Seen as Socialistic Force |date=1933-02-16 |newspaper=Buffalo Evening News |page=3 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref> In June 1931, Brumbaugh was appointed vice chairman of the Income and the Home Committee of President [[Herbert Hoover]]'s Conference on Home Building and Home Ownership.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-buffalo-news-two-from-u-b-honored/175021783/ |title=Two from U. B. Honored |date=1931-06-26 |newspaper=Buffalo Evening News |page=20 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref> In April 1933, he argued the [[Home Owners' Loan Corporation]]'s bill would increase obligations on the home owner, instead of decreasing them, as the bill intended.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-buffalo-news-success-of-home-owners/175033524/ |title=Success of Home-Owners Loan Bill is Held Doubtful |date=1933-04-27 |newspaper=Buffalo Evening News |page=18 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref> In 1937, he was chairman of the housing committee of the Buffalo City Planning Association.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-buffalo-news-subsidies-opposed-for-l/175034476/ |title=Subsidies Opposed for Low-Cost Housing |date=1937-03-24 |newspaper=Buffalo Evening News |page=19 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref>

In September 1943, Brumbaugh taught alongside [[W. Edwards Deming]], [[Holbrook Working]], [[Andrew I. Peterson]] and [[Edwin G. Olds]] a one-week course entitled "Quality Control by Statistical Methods".<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-buffalo-news-one-week-course-designe/175035319/ |title=One-Week Course Designed for Production Chiefs |date=1943-09-08 |newspaper=Buffalo Evening News |page=24 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref> In July 1944, he became editor and vice president of ''Industrial Quality Control'', a bi-monthly publication by the Buffalo Society of Quality Control Engineers.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-buffalo-news-society-begins-publicat/175035439/ |title=Society Begins Publication of Quality Control Data |date=1944-08-07 |newspaper=Buffalo Evening News |page=18 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref><ref name="asq">{{Cite web |url=https://asq.org/about-asq/honorary-members/brumbaugh |title=Martin A. Brumbaugh |website=[[American Society for Quality]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}</ref> He remained editor of the publication for three years.<ref name="rochester">{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-post-standard-quality-control-prize/175037245/ |title=Quality Control Prize to Honor Dr. Brumbaugh |date=1948-09-27 |newspaper=[[The Post-Standard]] |page=6 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref> In 1946, he is credited with helping merge the Federation of Quality Control Societies, which included the Buffalo Society of Quality Control Engineers and the ''Industrial Quality Control'' publication, with the 13-member Society for Quality Control into the [[American Society for Quality Control]]. Following the merger, he continued his role as editor of ''Industrial Quality Control'' and became chair of the editorial board. He remained in these roles until April 1947.<ref name="asq"/> In 1950, he was elected as the first vice president of the society.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-buffalo-news-quality-control-group-t/175036199/ |title=Quality Control Group to Mark 50th Year |date=1996-10-27 |newspaper=The Buffalo News |page=28 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-post-standard-dr-martin-a-brumbaug/175037501/ |title=Dr. Martin A. Brumbaugh... |date=1950-09-07 |newspaper=[[The Post-Standard]] |page=5 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref> He served as vice president until 1951.<ref name="asq"/>

In January 1947, Brumbaugh resigned from the University of Buffalo to become director of quality control of penicillin production and special assistant to vice president P. I. Bowman at Bristol Laboratories in [[Syracuse, New York|Syracuse]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-buffalo-news-a-position-as-director/175035673/ |title=A position as director of quality control... |date=1947-01-25 |newspaper=Buffalo Evening News |page=2 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-post-standard-dr-brumbaugh-joins-br/175036590/ |title=Dr. Brumbaugh Joins Bristol Labs |date=1947-03-09 |newspaper=[[The Post-Standard]] |page=32 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref> By 1951, he was director of statistics at Bristol Laboratories.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-buffalo-news-statistics-sessions-at/175035896/ |title=Statistics Sessions at U. B. to Attract 2 Once on Faculty |date=1951-05-26 |newspaper=Buffalo Evening News |page=6 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref>

In 1943, Brumbaugh was elected vice president of the Juniata College Alumni Association.<ref name="alumni"/>

==Works==
* Brumbaugh, Martin A. ''A Direct Method of Determining Cyclical Fluctuations of Economic Data''<ref name="buffalo"/>
* Brumbaugh, Martin A., Riegel, Robert (1935) ''Study Problems in Business Statistics''<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-buffalo-news-profs-martin-a-brumba/175033716/ |title=Profs. Martin A. Brumbaugh and Robert Riegel |date=1935-10-25 |newspaper=Buffalo Evening News |page=16 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref>
* Brumbaugh, Martin A., Kellogg, Lester S. (1940) ''Business Statistics''<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-buffalo-news-u-b-professor-is-auth/175034915/ |title=U. B. Professor is Author of Business Textbook |date=1941-09-20 |newspaper=Buffalo Evening News |page=3 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Brumbaugh married. He had at least one daughter and son, Joan Elizabeth and James Irvin.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-buffalo-news-miss-brumbaugh-plans-la/175056515/ |title=Miss Brumbaugh Plans Late June Nuptials |date=1951-04-02 |newspaper=Buffalo Evening News |page=10 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/syracuse-herald-journal-to-wed-16-may-1/175056695/ |title=To Wed |date=1957-05-16 |newspaper=Syracuse Herald-Journal |page=3 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-22}}{{Open access}}</ref> He lived on Lincoln Park Drive in Syracuse.<ref name="rochester"/>

==Awards and legacy==
In 1948, the Martin A. Brumbaugh Award was named in his honor by the Rochester Society for Quality Control and was established as an annual award for the most valuable article published in ''Industrial Quality Control''.<ref name="rochester"/> The Brumbaugh Award continued in the succeeding publications to ''Industrial Quality Control'', both ''Quality Progress'' and the ''Journal of Quality Technology''.<ref name="asq"/> In 1950, he received the [[Shewhart Medal]]. In 1960, he became the third honorary member of the American Society for Quality Control.<ref name="asq"/>
